name: Finland
sub: Waste Act separate collection of biowaste and packaging (cardboard, glass, metal, plastic) plus paper, with Rinki eco-points and HSY/Sortti rules.

banana.w: Fruit peels are biowaste and become biogas and compost.

eggshell.w: Egg shells go in biowaste with other kitchen scraps.

coffee.w: Coffee grounds and paper filters both go in biowaste.

bones.w: Bones and fish bones are accepted in Finnish biowaste.

shampoo.w: Empty plastic bottles go in plastic packaging collection.

polybag.w: Plastic bags are plastic packaging; they also work as a bag for other plastic packaging.

chips.w: Foil-lined crisp packets are mostly plastic, so they go in plastic packaging.

tube.w: Squeeze out what you can; plastic tubes go in plastic packaging, metal ones in metal.

carton.w: Milk and juice cartons go in cardboard packaging (kartonki); rinse and flatten them.

eggtray.w: Egg trays go with cardboard packaging; HSY also accepts them in biowaste.

box.w: Flatten cardboard boxes into cardboard packaging collection.

pizza.w: HSY accepts slightly greasy pizza boxes as cardboard; scrape off food, and very dirty ones go to mixed.

newspaper.w: Newspapers go in paper collection, separate from cardboard packaging.

jar.w: Empty glass jars go in glass packaging; put the metal lid in metal.

wine.w: Non-deposit wine bottles go in glass packaging; deposit bottles go back to the shop.

perfume.w: An empty perfume bottle counts as glass packaging; loose caps go elsewhere.

tin.w: Empty food tins go in metal collection.

window.w: Wrap small window shards and put them in mixed waste; whole windows go to a Sortti station.

drinkglass.w: Drinking glasses melt differently from bottles, so they go in mixed waste, not glass.

mirror.w: Mirror glass is not packaging and its coating harms recycling, so it goes in mixed waste.

tissue.w: In HSY's area and many others, used tissues and paper towels go in biowaste.

diaper.w: Nappies go in mixed waste, which is burned for energy.

pad.w: Sanitary pads go in mixed waste.

battery.w: Batteries are hazardous; any shop selling them has a free collection box.

bulb.w: Energy-saving bulbs contain mercury; take them to a hazardous or electrical waste point.

meds.w: Pharmacies take back household medicines and needles for free.

paint.w: A part-full paint can is hazardous; only an empty, dried can may go with metal.

toy.w: Finnish plastic collection is for packaging only, so plastic toys go in mixed waste.
